strengths: The paper addresses a significant practical bottleneck in diffusion LLM inference with a simple, training-free method. Combining approximate prefix/suffix KV caching with confidence-based parallel decoding is useful for existing bidirectional models without retraining.

The empirical gains are substantial and reasonably broad: two model families, four reasoning/code benchmarks, and multiple generation lengths. Tables 1–2 report combined throughput improvements of approximately 2.8–11×, generally with modest accuracy changes.

The component ablations demonstrate that caching and parallel decoding provide complementary benefits. Figure 5 also provides meaningful evidence that adaptive confidence thresholds outperform fixed token counts at comparable average decoding parallelism.

The paper supplies algorithmic pseudocode, hyperparameter sweeps, and an explicit theoretical analysis. The high-confidence joint-mode result gives a useful sufficient condition for understanding when independent token selection can work.
weaknesses: The deployment and autoregressive-competitiveness claims exceed the evaluation. Timing uses a single A100, batch size one, and no inference acceleration frameworks; the AR comparison is limited to one GSM8K configuration. Batched throughput, memory use, and comparisons with optimized AR serving are needed to establish practical competitiveness. Fixed-step diffusion comparisons are also concentrated on one benchmark.

The theoretical guarantee does not directly cover the implemented decoder. It assumes predictions are consistent marginals of a coherent joint distribution, which Appendix A acknowledges need not hold. Moreover, the default threshold of 0.9 does not enforce the theorem's token-count-dependent condition when more than nine tokens are selected. The displayed result concerns joint MAP, rather than directly establishing equivalence to the actual sequential neural decoding procedure.

Accuracy preservation is overstated. In Table 4 at length 512, accuracy falls from 78.9 to 74.8 with PrefixCache and 75.4 with DualCache. Table 3 also shows a 2.3-point loss for 5-shot DualCache. No repeated runs or confidence intervals are provided to substantiate claims of negligible degradation or small improvements.

The headline 27.6× figure is a throughput ratio, not the sample-latency reduction implied by Figure 1(c)'s end-to-end speedup labeling. Its displayed latencies decrease from 266 to approximately 12 seconds, roughly 22×. Reporting output lengths, aggregation procedures, and separate latency and throughput ratios would make the comparison clearer. Increasing maximum generation length also lowers absolute throughput, despite increasing relative speedup.

The cache approximation is supported mainly by downstream accuracy and averaged activation cosine similarity. High similarity alone does not establish small attention-output or prediction errors, and averaging can obscure sensitive layers or positions. Broader DualCache evaluation and direct measurements of prediction drift would strengthen this central component.

Novelty and reproducibility need sharper treatment. The paper acknowledges prior block-wise caching and confidence-based token selection, but provides limited positioning against related inference methods. Experimental details such as decoding temperature, precision, baseline step/block schedules, timing protocol, and the hyperparameter-selection procedure are insufficiently specified.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical bottleneck with a simple, training-free method. Block-wise approximate prefix/suffix KV caching and confidence-threshold decoding can be applied to existing bidirectional diffusion models without retraining.

Tables 1–2 provide substantial positive evidence across two models, four benchmarks, and two generation lengths. Combined acceleration reaches 3.7–11.0× on LLaDA and approximately 2.8–7.8× on Dream, generally with modest accuracy changes.

Component ablations demonstrate that caching and parallel decoding each contribute useful gains and combine effectively. Additional experiments examine cache block size, confidence threshold, prompt length, generation length, and suffix caching.

Figure 5 directly compares adaptive decoding with fixed-token-per-step alternatives and supports a better accuracy–computation tradeoff on GSM8K. The idealized theoretical analysis supplies a useful rationale for prioritizing high-confidence predictions.
weaknesses: The theoretical guarantee does not directly establish the safety of the implemented decoder. It assumes predictions are consistent marginals of a coherent joint distribution, an assumption explicitly acknowledged as idealized in Appendix A and not empirically validated. Moreover, the fixed threshold does not enforce the theorem’s dependence on the number of simultaneously decoded tokens: at threshold 0.9, the stated sufficient condition covers at most nine tokens, while Algorithm 1 imposes no such cap.

The headline speedup needs more precise interpretation. Figure 1c reports latencies of 266 seconds and 12 seconds, corresponding to approximately 22.2× latency reduction, whereas 27.6× is the ratio of reported token throughputs. Changes in generated output length can separate these metrics. Reporting output lengths, stopping behavior, aggregate timing methodology, and matched-workload latency would make the acceleration claim more convincing.

The practical deployment and autoregressive-competitiveness claims exceed the evaluation. Experiments use a single A100 and batch size one without inference acceleration frameworks. Autoregressive comparisons are limited to one plotted setting, and fixed-step decoding comparisons are concentrated on GSM8K. Optimized baselines, broader accuracy–latency frontiers, batching, and memory measurements are needed to substantiate deployment claims.

Accuracy preservation is overstated in some settings. In Table 4 at length 512, accuracy decreases from 78.9 to 74.8 with PrefixCache and to 75.4 with DualCache. Table 3 also shows a 2.3-point decrease for five-shot DualCache. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run analysis establish whether smaller reported changes are negligible.

The cache justification remains largely observational: averaged activation cosine similarity does not establish small attention-output or prediction errors, particularly across layers and difficult examples. Positioning against existing block-diffusion caching and confidence-based non-autoregressive decoding also needs sharper differentiation. Reproduction would benefit from explicit decoding temperatures, software versions, timing procedures, and hyperparameter-selection details.

Moreover, a fixed 0.9 threshold does not enforce the condition (n+1)ε≤1 when many tokens are decoded simultaneously. Deployment claims exceed the evaluated setting: measurements use one A100 and batch size one without inference acceleration frameworks. Optimized autoregressive comparisons, batching experiments, and memory measurements are needed to establish practical competitiveness.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical bottleneck with a simple, training-free combination of approximate bidirectional KV caching and adaptive parallel decoding.
Tables 1–2 provide convincing evidence across two model families and four benchmarks: combined throughput gains range from 2.8× to 11×, generally with modest accuracy changes.

Component ablations demonstrate complementary benefits from caching and parallel decoding. Comparisons against fixed-token decoding, cache-size sweeps, and threshold sweeps help establish why the approach works.
Additional experiments on DualCache, LLaDA-1.5, and multimodal tasks broaden the empirical support. The explicit algorithm and idealized theoretical analysis improve interpretability.
weaknesses: The theoretical guarantee does not directly cover the implemented decoder. It assumes consistent marginals of a common joint distribution, an assumption explicitly acknowledged as uncertain for MDMs. Approximate caching introduces further discrepancies. Fixed thresholds do not enforce the theorem’s token-count-dependent condition, and factors above one exceed its guaranteed regime.

The headline 27.6× result conflates throughput improvement with latency reduction. Figure 1(c) reports latency decreasing from 266 seconds to 12 seconds, approximately 22.2×, while 27.6× comes from the throughput ratio. Output-length differences, EOS handling, and timing aggregation need clearer accounting.

Claims of negligible accuracy loss are too broad. Table 5 shows GSM8K falling from 78.9 to 74.8 with PrefixCache and to 75.4 with DualCache; MathVista falls from 59.2 to 56.6. Confidence intervals or paired significance analyses are absent.

Deployment claims exceed the evaluation: primary results use batch size one without inference acceleration frameworks, while batched experiments examine caching alone on short outputs. Comparisons with optimized autoregressive serving and complete Fast-dLLM batching are needed.

Novelty positioning is incomplete. Block-wise caching and confidence-guided token selection have clear antecedents; the paper should more precisely distinguish its approximate cache reuse and adaptive selection from related approaches. Averaged KV cosine similarity also provides limited evidence about worst-case cache errors.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical bottleneck with a useful training-free combination of approximate bidirectional KV caching and confidence-adaptive parallel decoding. Applicability to existing checkpoints makes the contribution practically meaningful.
Tables 1–2 provide convincing evidence of complementary gains: combined acceleration reaches 3.7–11.0× on LLaDA and 2.8–7.8× on Dream across four benchmarks, generally with modest accuracy changes.

Component ablations, block-size and confidence sweeps, and comparisons against fixed tokens-per-step decoding help explain the gains. Additional experiments on LLaDA-1.5 and LLaDA-V provide evidence of transfer beyond the primary models.

The high-confidence theorem provides a useful idealized justification for adaptive parallelism, with an explicit proof and discussion of its consistency assumptions. The manuscript also acknowledges limitations at larger batch sizes.
weaknesses: The headline 27.6× result is a throughput ratio, but Figure 1 also describes it as end-to-end speedup while reporting latency decreasing from 266 to 12 seconds, approximately 22.2×. Output-length differences and aggregation conventions need clarification, together with precise timing and EOS-stopping procedures.

Claims of negligible accuracy loss are too broad. Table 5 shows GSM8K dropping from 78.9 to 74.8 with PrefixCache and to 75.4 with DualCache; MathVista drops from 59.2 to 56.6. Accuracy confidence intervals and a clearly specified validation protocol for choosing hyperparameters are missing.

The theoretical guarantee assumes coherent joint distributions whose marginals match the model predictions, an assumption explicitly acknowledged as approximate for practical MDMs. Fixed thresholds do not enforce the theorem's token-count-dependent condition, and factors above one relax its guarantee. Thus, the theory motivates the heuristic but does not establish reliable decoding for the implemented system.

Comparisons establish improvements over native diffusion inference more convincingly than competitiveness with optimized autoregressive serving. Figure 1 excludes inference acceleration frameworks, while the batch-size study evaluates caching alone on short outputs. Broader quality-matched comparisons and full-method batching measurements would strengthen the deployment claims.

Novelty positioning needs sharpening relative to existing block diffusion, activation reuse, and confidence-based non-autoregressive decoding. The dependency problem is already recognized in cited work, so identifying it should not itself be presented as a new discovery. Average KV cosine similarity also provides limited evidence about approximation errors in sensitive layers or difficult examples.
